verdicts.summary: Lean has a stronger form of it. The formula matches symbol for symbol: logPowerWeight (B j k) (P j k) (γ j k) r = B_{j,k}(1+|log r|)^{p_{j,k}} r^{γ_{j,k}} with Λ_log(q) = 1+|log q| as defined on p. 56, the bound (1/2)^j = 2^{-j}, the paper's 'any finite list of requirements' is a Finset tests j, the positivity γ_{j,k} > 0 of the display is the hypothesis hγ, and the range 0 < q ≤ a_j^{-1} that (5.40) inherits from (5.37) is written out as 0 < r ≤ 1/(a j). Lean is stronger in one respect: it bounds the absolute value, |B Λ_log^P q^γ| ≤ 2^{-j}, for arbitrary real B and P, which implies the paper's unsigned inequality; the converse would need B_{j,k} ≥ 0. exists_finite_diagonal_cut_bounds_with_tests additionally delivers one schedule meeting these tests and the (5.37) cut bounds simultaneously, which is what the paper's sentence ('the same cutoff choices can meet further normalized estimates') asserts.
